A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UME-R1. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMEB-V1/V2 evaluations, training ablations, repeated-sampling experiments, and qualitative retrieval examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds training-cost measurements and inference-throughput results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The embedding-token architecture, SFT losses, GRPO training, reward design, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Replacing 'generative embeddings' with 'reasoning-driven generative embeddings' clarifies terminology without changing the method.

E1.justification: Training sources and MMEB-V1/V2 task coverage are retained. The new throughput evaluation reuses CIRR, FashionIQ, K700, and MSVD, which already appear in v1, without introducing new data domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, ablations, and DUME/DUME+Gen/UME-R1 comparison in Figure 4. The added cost analysis uses existing DUME and UME-R1 embedding modes rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix B adds throughput evaluation in samples per second using vLLM on one L40s GPU, with image/video batch sizes of 8/4. Existing training and accuracy-evaluation protocols remain unchanged; the newly reported GPU-hours do not establish a change in training budgets.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds an efficiency analysis comparing training costs and generative versus discriminative inference throughput. Existing reward ablations, inference-time sampling analysis, retrieval cases, and training-trajectory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The pass@k sampling description and unbiased estimator are unchanged. The new cost results introduce no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy tables and plotted results are unchanged. v2 newly reports 1,487 H20 GPU-hours for DUME and 2,336/1,344 for UME-R1 SFT/RL. New Table 4 adds throughput results, including 1.48 versus 20.0 samples/s on CIRR for generative versus discriminative embeddings. These are additional measurements, not between-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7), including the contrastive objectives, GRPO objective, advantage normalization, and embedding reward, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, proofs, or theoretical guarantees appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the pioneering/first-exploration claim from generative embeddings generally to reasoning-driven generative embeddings. The central claims about embedding complementarity, RL benefits, and inference-time scaling remain.

C2.justification: New Appendices A-B explicitly acknowledge computation costs and interpret throughput differences in terms of input length. The previously proposed future work on adaptive embedding selection is now also identified as an unresolved practical routing limitation. Expanded captions explain the retained retrieval examples more specifically.

D1.justification: v2 adds hardware, GPU-hour accounting, and the vLLM throughput setup. Its abstract changes a planned code/model/data release to stated availability at the same repository, although the reproducibility statement still says 'will release'; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 adds background references including AVG-LLaVA, multimodal-thought inference-time scaling, s1, and a state-transition framework for LLM reasoning. Novelty positioning becomes specific to reasoning-driven generative embeddings, while the existing comparison with embedding research is retained.

P1.justification: v2 refines terminology throughout, adds short limitations and cost appendices, expands example explanations, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, and the conference header. The LLM-use declaration moves from Appendix A to before the references. The main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds throughput Table 4, relocates Table 1 from page 6 to page 7, and renumbers the existing appendix tables. Captions for Figures 8-14 are expanded, with associated layout adjustments. Existing diagrams, plots, and case panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The new cost measurements and explicit limitations make the performance-versus-computation tradeoff clearer and better qualify the practical significance of oracle results. Narrower novelty wording and fuller case explanations improve precision. These are useful but limited gains: the core method and accuracy evidence remain unchanged, and the resource-release statements remain inconsistent.
